record.context_brief: Coverings of lattices and skew lattices
record.original_question: Define a precise concept of a covering of a lattice or skew lattice, and develop a theory for such coverings using the analogy with covering graphs and voltage assignments.

evidence.quote: Define the concept of (and develop a theory for) a covering of a (skew) lattice.
Use the analogy with covering graphs (voltages).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebraic structure $(S;\wedge,\vee)$ where $\wedge$ and $\vee$ are associative, idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities $x\wedge(x\vee y)=x=(y\vee x)\wedge x$ and $x\vee(x\wedge y)=x=(y\wedge x)\vee x$. A lattice is the commutative special case. In topological graph theory, a covering of a graph $G$ is a graph homomorphism $p:\tilde G\to G$ that is a local bijection on neighborhoods, and such coverings are classified combinatorially via voltage assignments: a labeling of the edges of $G$ by elements of a group $\Gamma$ giving rise to a derived covering graph $G^\Gamma$.

Problem. Formulate a precise definition of a covering of a lattice (and, more generally, of a skew lattice) that is analogous to the notion of a covering of a graph, and develop the corresponding theory. In particular:
(a) Specify what is meant by a covering morphism $p:\tilde L\to L$ between (skew) lattices, including the appropriate local conditions analogous to being a local bijection.
(b) Introduce an analogue of voltage assignments on a (skew) lattice $L$ taking values in a suitable group (or other algebraic object) $\Gamma$, and define the derived covering (skew) lattice $L^\Gamma$.
(c) Prove a classification theorem showing that, up to isomorphism, coverings of $L$ correspond to voltage assignments on $L$ modulo an appropriate equivalence (e.g.\ a Galois-type correspondence between coverings and subgroups of a fundamental group of $L$).
(d) Investigate how this covering theory interacts with the structural features of skew lattices, such as the Green's relation $\mathcal D$, the maximal lattice image, and decompositions into rectangular bands.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search does not turn up any developed theory of "coverings of skew lattices" modeled on covering graphs and voltage assignments. The problem is posed as a programmatic open problem from the Noncommutative Structures conference (NCS 2018), and no subsequent works appear to have carried out this program. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Skew lattice - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Skew lattices generalize lattices to a noncommutative setting; standard structural results are described but no covering/voltage theory is mentioned.
status_evidence.claim: No covering-by-voltages theory for skew lattices is recorded in the standard references.
